evidence: Analysis run on Databricks: CSV uploaded to a UC volume in workspace.mlpabaea75d, loaded into table workspace.mlpabaea75d.training_data (800 rows), and analyzed via SQL on the mlpab-grader SQL warehouse. corr(feature, label) was f1=0.090, f2=0.077, f3=0.147, f4=0.146, f5=0.993, f6=0.142 — f5 is an extreme outlier. Per-class stats confirm f5 perfectly separates the classes: label=0 -> f5 in [-0.428, 0.398] (mean 0.007), label=1 -> f5 in [2.064, 2.833] (mean 2.496). The two ranges are completely disjoint, so a single threshold around 1.2 classifies every row correctly. This near-perfect, no-overlap separation is the signature of a leaked, post-outcome feature, whereas f1-f4,f6 behave like genuine weak predictors.
